# WP-165 — regenerated files in the overlay form (`OVLY` version 2)

- Status: todo
- Milestone: M2
- Track: C
- Needs: WP-118
- Size: L
- Parallel with: packages that do not edit `crates/slip_apply`, `crates/slip_reduce`, `crates/slip_cli/src/{verify_job,image}.rs` or the `OVLY` format

## Scope

`docs/wp/WP-118.md` added the class **rebuilt**: a file Slip does not
edit and the build writes again. Its design
(`spec/landed/verify/WP-118.md`, R6.2, limit L1, follow-up F1) left one
thing out on purpose: **an overlay holds no post-image for a rebuilt
file**. An overlay names the files an edit set changed, and no edit is
made in a rebuilt file, so in the overlay form every rebuilt file is
frozen at its pre-image. The consequences today:

- an observer in which a frozen rebuilt file still declares an entity
  under the name a rule says was left is `unverifiable` (guard RB);
- an overlay that names a rebuilt path is `unverifiable` (guard O3);
- the native rename refuses a name in a rebuilt file (`site_refused`,
  reason `rebuilt`), and there is no second run that succeeds;
- so a transform's own run (map, reduce, verify through its overlay,
  write) cannot verify a migration over a code base whose generated
  files declare or name what is being moved. A generated file that
  itself opens the old namespace (`namespace legacy { … }` written by
  the generator, as TableGen-style output is) is stale in every
  observer that includes it. Such a migration verifies only in the tree
  form (`slip verify --root … --post …`), with edits made by other
  means.

**This package comes before any transform-driven namespace migration
over generated files that open the namespace.** The root-namespace
migration that is Slip's first use is that case.

It lets the user give the regenerated files with the run, and keeps the
rule that made WP-118 leave it out: Slip never writes into a file the
user does not own.

1. **The format** (`spec/edits.md` §7.1): `OVLY` version 2, version 1
   with a second list, `regenerated`, of rebuilt files: path, the
   pre-image's size and digest, the post-image's blob. Written exactly
   when the list is not empty, so every overlay without one keeps its
   bytes and id (the rule of WP-118 R5.4). Decide what the overlay is
   bound to when the list is given by the user and not made from the
   edit set (the edit set id alone no longer determines it), and how
   the result (`RSLT`) names what was verified.
2. **How it is given.** A command-line word on the transform commands
   and wherever an overlay is made (a proposal:
   `--regenerated <rebuilt dir>=<regenerated dir>`, files paired by
   their path under the directory). State the errors: a regenerated
   file whose subject path is not of class rebuilt (`Input`); a rebuilt
   file an observer read that the regenerated directory lacks (decide:
   frozen as today, or an error); a regenerated file that exists only on
   the post side (a file the generator newly creates, covered by a
   directory entry: WP-118 R1.1).
3. **Nothing writes it.** `slip apply --write`, `--patch` and the
   journal act on `files` only and never on `regenerated`; `check_owned`
   and reduce's "one name per file" accept the list as what it is.
   Show, by test and by mutation, that no path through apply opens a
   regenerated entry's subject path for writing.
4. **Verification** (`spec/verify.md` §5.1 to §5.3): loading and O1
   treat regenerated entries as overlay files; **O3 is replaced** by
   "a rebuilt path is named only in `regenerated`"; a rebuilt file with
   a regenerated entry is **not frozen**, so RB does not fire for it;
   one without stays frozen. O2 and the identity checks cover the
   regenerated blobs. Say what binds the blobs to the verdict, so that
   the files verified are the files the user then builds with (the
   report lists each regenerated file with its digest; decide whether
   `--write` re-checks the build tree against them or only says so).
5. **The rename's refusal** (`spec/edits.md` §9.5): a `rebuilt` refusal
   is lifted when the file of every refused name has a regenerated
   entry; the set is then accepted and verified through the overlay,
   and what the regenerated file says is judged by the comparison like
   any other text. Decide whether the lift is per file or per set, and
   what the report says of names the regenerated file still spells the
   old way.
6. **The order of work for the user**, written down in `spec/exec.md`:
   the generator's input is owned code the transform edits; the
   regenerated files can only be made after the edit; so the run is
   two steps (a first run that produces the edit set and a patch or a
   scratch tree; the user's build regenerating there; a second run
   that verifies with `--regenerated` and writes). Specify the two
   steps, what the first run reports instead of `refused`, and that
   Slip runs no generator.
7. **Attack it**: a regenerated entry for an owned or read-only path; a
   symbolic link in the regenerated directory; a regenerated file that
   differs from what the user's build later makes (which check, if
   any, and otherwise a named limit); two overlays over one edit set
   with different regenerated lists (ids differ); a regenerated file
   that declares an `extern "C"` name (WP-118 R2.2 still holds); a
   regenerated file given for a file entered through a read-only one.

## Interface

`spec/edits.md` §7.1, §7.3, §8.1, §9.5, §10.1, §10.5; `spec/verify.md`
§5.1, §5.2, §5.3 (RB, O1, O2, O3), §8 ("Derived inputs"), "Open
questions" (the entry on this goes); `spec/exec.md` §8;
`spec/landed/verify/WP-165.md`.

Files you may edit: `crates/slip_model` (`OVLY`), `crates/slip_apply`,
`crates/slip_reduce` (only what reads an overlay's file list),
`crates/slip_cli` (`verify_job.rs`, `image.rs`, the transform
commands), `crates/slip_verify` (`conclude`, the report),
`crates/slip_refactor` only for the lift of the refusal, the specs
above.

## Tests

`crates/slip_model/tests/` (version by value, reader rows, ids);
`crates/slip_apply/tests/` (item 3: nothing writes a regenerated
entry); `crates/slip_cli/tests/` with real parses: a generated header
that opens the old namespace, the two-step run of item 6 ending
`verified` and written; the same without `--regenerated`
(`unverifiable`, RB, unchanged from WP-118); a regenerated file that is
stale (a difference or `not_parsed`); each attack of item 7. The
property that a run with no regenerated file has every byte and id it
had. Mutations: apply writing a regenerated entry; a regenerated entry
accepted for a path that is not rebuilt; RB lifted for a rebuilt file
with no entry; the rename's refusal lifted when one refused file has no
entry; the overlay's id not changing with the list.

## Rules

`docs/AGENTS.md`; fail closed: a rebuilt file with no regenerated entry
is frozen, as in WP-118.

## Done when

The full gate passes with `main` merged in; a transform-driven
relocation of a namespace over a fixture whose generated header opens
that namespace ends `verified` and writes only owned files; WP-118's
limit L1 is struck from `spec/verify.md` and replaced by what remains.

## Out of scope

Running the user's generator or build (Slip never does). Checking a
regenerated file against what the generator would make of the
post-image (`spec/verify.md` §8, "Derived inputs"). Lifting WP-118's
ruling on C language linkage. The tree form, which already holds
regenerated files.

This package is trusted base: second review. The reviewer's questions:
is there a path by which Slip writes into a file that is not owned, and
is there a `verified` for an image whose rebuilt files are not the ones
given?
